name: A. V. Anokhin National Museum
full: A. V. Anokhin National Museum of the Altai Republic — Gorno-Altaysk, 46 Grigory Choros-Gurkin St.
near: Gorno-Altaysk (city centre; 5–7 min on foot from the bus station, ~15 min from Lenin Square)
short: The main museum of the Altai Mountains: archaeology from the Stone Age to the ancient Turks, the “Ukok Princess” — the mummy of a Pazyryk woman about 2,500 years old — Altai ethnography and paintings by G. I. Choros-Gurkin.
desc: The museum is named after the Turkologist and ethnographer Andrey Viktorovich Anokhin. The new building opened in 2012 after a major reconstruction funded with help from Gazprom. The collection holds more than 60,000 items; the permanent exhibitions are ancient history (7 halls), ethnography (3), nature (4, including mammoth bones), the “Ukok Plateau” complex with a reconstructed burial, fine art (3 halls, including works by Choros-Gurkin) and modern history (6 halls). The centrepiece is the mummy of the “Ukok Princess” (Pazyryk culture, 6th–2nd centuries BC), found on Ukok in 1993. She is displayed only on certain days according to a lunar calendar agreed with Altai traditions (waxing moon), from 09:30 to 13:00 under strict climate control; flash photography and video are prohibited. There is an audio guide (Russian, Altai, English), themed tours, a museum shop, a cafe and a research library; the Pushkin Card is accepted. In 2026 the entrance is at the end of the building because the main staircase is under repair.
guide: Check the dates: the “Ukok Princess” is shown only 9–10 days a month and only until 13:00 — on other days you will see the reconstructed burial but not the mummy itself. Look at the tattoos on her shoulder (mythical griffin-deer) — they are often compared to modern tattoos. Many Altai people believe that removing the princess from Ukok brought earthquakes to the republic, which is why the showings are timed to a “favourable” moon. Do not skip the hall with Choros-Gurkin’s paintings — after them you see Belukha and the Katun differently.
see: The “Ukok Plateau” complex and the mummy of the “Ukok Princess” (on display days); the ancient history halls (Pazyryk burial mounds, ancient Turkic stone statues); Altai ethnography (ail, costumes, shamanic items); the nature section (mammoth, fauna); paintings by G. I. Choros-Gurkin.
skip: You have only one day in Altai and the weather is great — nature matters more; or you will not be there on a mummy display day and are not interested in archaeology.
diff: None (city museum; 2–3 h to see it).
when: Year-round; ideally on mummy display days (2026: 14–18, 21–25 October; 11–15, 18–22 November; 11–12, 16–20, 23–24 December; September — 16–20, 23–26).
hours: Wed–Sat 9:30–17:30, Sun 9:30–16:30, closed Mon–Tue (2GIS, 10.2026); per snovatrip/karoaltai — Wed–Sat until 18:00, Sun until 17:00, ticket offices close 30 min earlier. The mummy is shown only on display days, 09:30–13:00.
daytime: Morning (9:30–13:00) is the only time the mummy is shown.
how: The museum is in the centre of Gorno-Altaysk: 5–7 min on foot from the bus station, ~15 min from Lenin Square. From Gorno-Altaysk airport — taxi across the city. From Belokurikha it is 122 km (bus/taxi); from Manzherok ~38 km, from Chemal ~100 km (karoaltai).
needcar: No, if you are already in Gorno-Altaysk; otherwise take a bus/taxi to the city.
traveltime: From the bus station 5–7 min on foot; from Manzherok ~40 min; from Chemal ~2 h.
stay: Hotels and guesthouses in Gorno-Altaysk and Maima (specific prices were not collected — outside the scope).
net: City — all operators (MTS, Beeline, MegaFon, Tele2), not checked separately.
entry: Adult 350 ₽, full-time students 200 ₽, pensioners and schoolchildren 150 ₽, family ticket 750 ₽ (2 adults + 1–3 children aged 7–16), children under 7 free (2GIS, updated 27.03.2026; snovatrip 2026). Audio guide 350 ₽. There is a separate ticket for viewing the mummy (official website; price not found). The Pushkin Card is accepted. Tourist tax applies only when staying overnight in Gorno-Altaysk.
transfer: City tour 2700 ₽ (Sputnik8); tour with transfer from Manzherok/Chemal from 2850 ₽ (KARO).
bring: Passport/Pushkin Card for discounts, cash/card; a warm sweater — the mummy hall is +16…18 °C.
warn: The mummy is shown only on schedule and until 13:00; flash photography and video are prohibited in its hall. The museum is closed Mon–Tue. In 2026 the entrance is at the end of the building (staircase repairs).
food: The museum cafe serves regional dishes, including yak and maral (Altai deer) meat (snovatrip); in town there are cafes with Altai cuisine (kyoche, talkan, kai-chai).
reviews: 2GIS: 4.9/5, 1,834 ratings, 598 reviews (10.2026). Pros — rich archaeology, the Ukok princess, modern exhibition. Cons — the mummy is not visible every day, entrance under repair.

p.sum: A city museum in the centre of Gorno-Altaysk, 5–7 minutes on foot from the bus station. Wed–Sun, entry 350 ₽. The main thing is to time your visit for a “Ukok Princess” display day (9–10 days a month, only 9:30–13:00).
